limited_overlap.description: 835 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 77,460 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
164 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10068 of 12000 applicants answered (83.9%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.34 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0012, causal_forest=-0.0003.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -7.6; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = 0.84. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 3468 (90% -3893 to 10828).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 3424 (90% 2531 to 4317); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4280, without months_unemployed = 3727, without education = 3979; full model = 3794.
Run time 11 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10068.
